name: Solanum
common_group: Nightshades (including horsenettles, buffalobur and cultivated tomato)

project_scope.study_context: Central Texas Hays County source-pool visual identification
project_scope.admission: All seven already canonical; no new taxa installed during this genus pass.
project_scope.science_gate: Retain PROVISIONAL county labels for unverified county-native species; bittersweet COMPARISON_NONNATIVE and tomato COMPARISON_CULTIGEN excluded from native counts.
project_scope.media_gate: 11 species media files physically installed total; 9 rights-cleared photos in this genus public teaching gallery from five species, with CC BY-NC dimidiatum and UT rights-unverified triquetrum held out of public reuse.

look_here_first: Look at the FLOWER'S five petals joined into a star and the YELLOW ANTHERS clustered near the center; inspect their terminal openings with magnifier if possible. Then check STEM PRICKLES and LEAF HAIRS, whether leaves are silver/narrow or green/broad, whether flowers have UNEQUAL anthers, and whether the fruit is a black/red/yellow BERRY or is concealed inside a PRICKLY enlarged calyx. Avoid flower COLOR or berry COLOR alone as identification.

genus_diagnostics.flower: A five-parted usually star/rotate COROLLA (petals united at base) and five stamens, often with long yellow anthers clustered around central style. Colors and flower sizes vary widely, and some wild species have unequal anthers.
genus_diagnostics.anthers: Solanum often has PORICIDAL anthers: pollen escapes through little terminal pores; in some unarmed species those pores expand into longitudinal slits. Inspect anther shape, length and whether one is much longer: buffalobur has conspicuous unequal anthers (heteranthery). Ordinary front-flower photos do not resolve a pore.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Mostly alternate, simple to lobed or divided; several spiny horsenettles have star-shaped (STELLATE) surface hairs. Silverleaf nightshade has dense silvery scale-like hairs and narrow leaves; tomato has deeply divided foliage; scrambling S. triquetrum often has triangular/hastate leaves.
genus_diagnostics.stems: Some plants are UNARMED, some are prickly. Prickles are sharp epidermal emergences, NOT true branch thorns. Inspect stems, leaf veins, leaf underside and calyx; prickle number varies with age and individual.
genus_diagnostics.calyx: CALYX = outer SEPALS immediately below the corolla. In some Solanum it stays as a collar around an exposed berry; in S. americanum ripe calyx lobes bend far backward; in S. rostratum the fruiting calyx becomes enlarged and densely spiny enclosing the dry berry.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Solanum fruits are generally berries with multiple seeds: shiny black, shiny red, yellow-orange or variable domesticated tomato berries. Buffalobur encloses its dry berry with a prickly calyx, whereas silverleaf nightshade shows green-striped juvenile berries and later yellow-orange fruit. Never classify unknown berries as edible by fruit color.
genus_diagnostics.pollination: Most Solanum anther morphology is associated with vibration/buzz release of pollen by bees; do not infer pollinator identity from the flower image or treat it as a native host-count assertion.

shared_traits: Solanaceae family: flowers typically have fused 5-part corolla, stamens attached to the corolla, persistent calyx and a multi-seeded berry or capsule.
Solanum genus: starry flower morphology and clustered anthers commonly opening through terminal pores or short slits, berry-type fruit, highly variable leaves and prickles.
Species key: examine fruiting CALYX and anther equality with leaf hair/shape and armature — never use corolla color alone.
priority: 1. SEE one front-view flower, identify star-shaped joined COROLLA and YELLOW ANTHERS.
2. SPOT a mature fruit AND calyx; black fruit with swept-back sepals, red fruit, or spiny calyx around fruit?
3. NAME the differences: stellate hairs, terminal anther pores, long curved anther, sepals/calyx, and berry.
4. COMPARE paired look-alikes: silverleaf/dimidiatum/buffalobur; triquetrum/dulcamara; americanum/other black nightshades.
5. REMEMBER 'Not all nightshades are poisonous look-alikes, and not every nightshade is native'. Keep botanical ID distinct from consumption and native-range claims.
warnings: Source photo geography and garden tomato shots do not establish Texas target-zone native occurrence.
Prickles and star-shaped petals are not individually necessary/sufficient for Solanum in all circumstances.
Existing dimidiatum photo CC BY-NC is for allowed study context only; existing triquetrum UT voucher license still REVIEW.
No arrows or pore-scale identifications are certified without inspecting the original photo pixels.

quick_key.if: Unarmed green herb, small white flowers, later glossy BLACK berries
quick_key.then: S. americanum candidate; tiny anthers + backward-bent ripe calyx are the best confirming structures. Check close black-nightshade relatives.

quick_key.if: Unarmed scrambling vine, PURPLE reflexed star flowers and red berry
quick_key.then: S. dulcamara — introduced comparison, do not count as native.

quick_key.if: Unarmed scrambling plant, WHITE/green-eyed star flowers, triangular to hastate leaves and red berry
quick_key.then: S. triquetrum — Texas nightshade; local photos rights pending.

quick_key.if: NARROW SILVERY leaves with dense tiny stellate hairs, violet flower, yellow/orange ripe berry
quick_key.then: S. elaeagnifolium — silverleaf nightshade; inspect silver leaf rather than flower color.

quick_key.if: Broad green lobed leaves, fairly robust stems with sparse-to-moderate long prickles, lavender flower and yellow fruit
quick_key.then: S. dimidiatum — Western horsenettle; stem/habit photo still pending.

quick_key.if: Very densely PRICKLY, deeply divided leaf, YELLOW flower with one conspicuously CURVED long anther and prickly fruiting calyx
quick_key.then: S. rostratum — buffalobur. Real flower + bur photos installed.

quick_key.if: Obviously cultivated tomato habit, divided leaves, yellow flowers and large variable berries
quick_key.then: S. lycopersicum — useful Solanum comparison, not native local flora.

comparison_cards.title: Prickly nightshades — Silverleaf vs Western horsenettle vs Buffalobur
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Look at the LEAVES and PRICKLES before deciding based on lavender/yellow color. Then look for the remarkably unequal anthers of buffalobur.

field_matrix.elaeagnifolium: Narrow, densely silver/gray scaly stellate hairs
field_matrix.dimidiatum: Broader, greener, variably lobed, generally robust
field_matrix.rostratum: Deeply divided lobes and heavily prickled foliage

field_matrix.elaeagnifolium: Usually blue/violet, five nearly equal yellow anthers
field_matrix.dimidiatum: Usually pale lavender/blue, approximately equal anthers
field_matrix.rostratum: Yellow, strongly UNEQUAL stamens; one long curved lower anther

field_matrix.elaeagnifolium: Green often striped when young, yellow/orange when mature
field_matrix.dimidiatum: Larger yellow berries commonly up to ~2.5 cm
field_matrix.rostratum: Dry brown berry concealed by highly prickly expanding calyx

field_matrix.dimidiatum: One existing flower view is CC BY-NC; stem/leaf/fruit macro needed
field_matrix.rostratum: Three exact installed photos include long-curved anther and fruiting calyx

comparison_cards.caution: Prickle density varies by individual and age, and silverleaf can be sparsely prickly. Prickles alone are not a genus-wide or species-wide yes/no key.

comparison_cards.title: Scrambling red-berried nightshades — Texas vs Bittersweet
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Both may scramble and bear red berries. Check leaf outline and flower petal COLOR WITH ANTHERS, and distinguish triangular/white versus ovate-to-lobed/purple.

field_matrix.triquetrum: Generally sharp triangular to hastate; highly variable
field_matrix.dulcamara: Generally ovate, often with basal lobes but less sharply triangular

field_matrix.triquetrum: White, sometimes slightly purple tinged, usually greenish-white shiny eye; equal anthers
field_matrix.dulcamara: Purple, swept-back petals with green/white eyes and equal anthers
Shiny red, so fruit COLOR alone fails

field_matrix.dulcamara: Non-native comparison (retain in learner; don't count native-only)

comparison_cards.caution: Texas nightshade has existing UT specimen photo but reuse rights unverified; do not silently use that photo as a public gallery image.

comparison_cards.title: Unarmed black nightshade vs tomato and other black-berried look-alikes
comparison_cards.look_here_first: For a small BLACK-BERRIED herb, confirm tiny WHITE flowers, very short ANTHERS and fruiting calyx lobes REFLEXED (bent backward). Do not use dark berry color alone to separate the Solanum nigrum complex.

field_matrix.americanum: Small white flowers (~4–8 mm), anthers usually 0.7–1.5 mm, shiny purplish-black berries; fruiting calyx bent strongly backward

field_matrix.lookalikes: S. emulans / S. nigrescens / S. nigrum complex may overlap. Hand-lens anther length, mature fruit calyx and internal hard granules can matter.

field_matrix.lycopersicum: Glandular hairy plant with divided foliage, yellow flowers and conspicuously larger variable cultivated berries

field_matrix.photos: Existing americanum photo is an unarmed green herb, not a fruit macro; Harry Rose Commons flower and fruit are external-only references.

comparison_cards.caution: Do not treat a ripe black berry as evidence that any unknown nightshade is edible. Toxicity varies; this is an identification lesson, not foraging advice.

visual_comparison.title: Solanum: seven nightshades — first inspect anthers, leaves and fruit coverings
visual_comparison.subtitle: Nine installed and visually checked genus example photos from five species, plus two explicitly EXTERNAL Commons references of American black nightshade. S. dimidiatum CC BY-NC and S. triquetrum UT restricted sources are omitted from this public-reuse genus gallery. No anther-pore macro or arrow is certified.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: STAR FLOWER + ANTHERS → LEAF HAIRS/PRICKLES → CALYX/FRUIT. SILVER narrow leaves, one LONG curved anther, BLACK berry with reflexed sepals or RED-berried triangular-leaf climber?

part_examples.title: 1 · SEE a real nightshade flower
part_examples.look_for: A violet star-shaped COROLLA surrounds five yellow anthers gathered near the central STYLE. 'Corolla' means all the joined petals; 'anther' is pollen-making part of a stamen. The terminal pores are too small to verify in this image.
part_examples.why_it_matters: The close floral architecture is a better genus clue than whether the flower is purple, white or yellow.

part_examples.title: 2 · SPOT unequal anthers on buffalobur
part_examples.look_for: Find ONE extra-long curved lower anther below the four shorter yellow anthers. This is HETERANTHERY (two anther forms in one flower), which helps distinguish buffalobur among the local prickly Solanum.
part_examples.why_it_matters: One of the best real installed species-level identification macros in this group.

part_examples.title: 3 · NAME the prickly calyx
part_examples.look_for: The CALYX is the green outer whorl of sepals. As buffalobur fruits mature the calyx enlarges (ACCRESCENT) and becomes a vicious prickly BUR around the actual berry. Distinguish sepal and fruit rather than calling the whole prickly structure a seed pod.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Separates a spiny covering from the enclosed fruit; more informative than yellow flower color.

part_examples.title: 4 · COMPARE silverleaf's surface and habit
part_examples.look_for: Whole plant with light silver narrow leaves. The silver comes from dense fine star-shaped (STELLATE), often scale-like hairs; the individual hair rays need a 1 mm microscope photo. Do not claim this distant photo resolves rays.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Separates silverleaf from greener, broad-leaved horsenettles even before flowers appear.

part_examples.title: 5 · FOLLOW flower to young striped berry
part_examples.look_for: Real round pale-green fruits with DARK GREEN STRIPES and persistent green sepals, surrounded by silvery foliage. These fruits are immature and are not evidence that ripe fruit stays striped.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Connects the ovary to a fleshy berry and distinguishes it from the prickly-bur fruit enclosure.

part_examples.title: 6 · Compare the scrambling purple-flowered vine
part_examples.look_for: Purple petals sweep backward around a bright yellow cluster of stamens; some leaves have small basal lobes. This is the introduced bittersweet comparison. Compare white-flowered Texas nightshade's sharply triangular leaves using an independently cleared image later.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Prevents conflating two scrambling red-berried Solanum species merely because both have greenish eye spots.

part_examples.title: 7 · Compare the small unarmed herb
part_examples.look_for: A spreading green herb with alternate ovate leaves and no prickles. Ripe black berries and the short anthers are too small or absent in THIS photo; open source-linked fruit and flower references in the genus comparison instead.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Distinguishes a black-berried unarmed species from rough prickly nightshades, while highlighting what's still missing.

part_examples.title: 8 · NEED PHOTO — Western horsenettle green prickles
part_examples.role: Solanum dimidiatum broad green leaves, stem prickles and mature fruit
part_examples.look_for: Rights-cleared exact S. dimidiatum whole plant showing cream-yellow stem prickles, comparatively broad green and lobed leaves, flower, and a mature yellow berry. The existing single CC BY-NC flower view is retained in private species gallery but not reused in this public lesson until commercial-use restrictions are resolved.
part_examples.why_it_matters: The common lavender flower is NOT enough to distinguish it from silverleaf. Need side-by-side same-angle leaf/stem views.

part_examples.title: 9 · NEED PHOTO — Texas nightshade versus bittersweet
part_examples.role: Solanum triquetrum leaf, flower eye, red berry
part_examples.look_for: A clear rights-cleared exact S. triquetrum same-plant sequence: triangular to hastate leaves, white sometimes purple-tinged corolla with greenish central eye, and shiny red berries. The currently installed UT herbarium voucher is private-study source with reuse permission not confirmed.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Makes the extremely realistic scrambling red-fruited look-alike pair identifiable with real photographic tie-breakers.

visual_comparison.annotation_policy: Photo subjects are real and metadata supported. Structure names are look-for cues only unless the actual visible image shows the feature. No manual arrow target positions validated; rights-gated source photos remain excluded.
